scope: Curated, primary-source register for active claims and data; not an exhaustive literature search. Historical larger catalogue is preserved separately.

sources.title: GEMS problem description and submission format
sources.used: requirements, objective definition and emission design

claims.statement: Newly identified expert faults comprise the initial test dataset; known labels are not hidden truth.
claims.quote: These new faults will comprise the test dataset for the initial prize round of the challenge.

claims.statement: Submit one float32 prediction band with confidence values between zero and one.
claims.quote: Your submission contains a single layer with datatype of 32-bit float

claims.statement: Use the training grid's 100 m resolution.
claims.quote: Your submission is at the same resolution as the training data (100m)

claims.statement: Projected coordinate system is UTM zone 11N / EPSG 32611.
claims.quote: EPSG 32611

claims.statement: The metric uses a linear distance kernel with 300 m support.
claims.quote: 300 meters (i.e., 3 pixels at 100m resolution)

claims.statement: Choose one final submission for both rounds without private scores.
claims.quote: Competitors must choose a single submission for scoring across both rounds before the deadline

claims.statement: The official page describes an all-absence sample, unlike the supplied mirror's positive values.
claims.quote: A sample submission that predicts total fault absence is provided for your reference

claims.statement: The metric is a distance-weighted Tversky index with alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 and a triangular kernel of 300 m support; TP_w/FP_w/FN_w are defined as maxima over the 300 m neighbourhood.
claims.quote: For this competition, we set 𝛼=0.2 and 𝛽=0.8, which reduces the penalty for false positive predictions and increases the penalty for false negative predictions.

claims.statement: The published worked example gives TP_w=3.00, FP_w=1.89, FN_w=2.00 and TI_w=0.60.

The Initial Prize Round scores against a private set of expert-labelled faults that are not in the public database; the Final Prize Round rescores the same single submission against an expanded label set.
claims.quote: These new faults have been manually labeled by fault experts and comprise the test dataset for the competition.

claims.statement: Supplied labels come from the USGS Quaternary fault maps and the INGENIOUS project.
claims.quote: The labels for this challenge come from the USGS quaternary fault maps and from INGENIOUS.

claims.statement: The data download includes 1m_DEM_links.csv listing URLs for 1 m-resolution DEM data.
claims.quote: you will find a CSV file called 1m_DEM_links.csv that contains links where DEM data at 1m resolution can be downloaded.

claims.statement: Distance weighting exists because rasterization is lossy and portions of the existing fault data may be misaligned from the true surface-fault location.
claims.quote: Rasterization is lossy and can induce off‑by‑one errors near pixel boundaries. In addition, portions of the existing fault data may be misaligned from the true location of the surface fault

sources.retrieved: 2026-09-25 (Arena research tool, both content chunks; equations and examples quoted verbatim)

External data are encouraged with the necessary licenses.
claims.quote: The use of external data is encouraged in this competition

claims.statement: Three submissions per week, subject to the current platform limit.
claims.quote: three submissions per week

claims.statement: Disclose the extent and manner of generative-AI use in the narrative.
claims.quote: indicate in the narrative

claims.statement: Finalists must provide complete solution code and documentation.
claims.quote: complete code assets and documentation

claims.statement: The rules direct competitors to the website for the current timeline.
claims.quote: Please see the competition website gems.drivendata.org for the most current timeline

claims.statement: Appendix A also contains a generic 5 p.m. ET deadline clause; flag rather than silently reconcile.
claims.quote: by 5:00 p.m. ET

sources.title: Cross-validation strategies for structured data (2017)
sources.role: motivation for blocked rather than random validation
sources.access: free article; publisher may restrict automated requests

claims.statement: The authors recommend blocked cross-validation for dependent data, with careful blocking design.
claims.quote: We recommend that block cross-validation be used wherever dependence structures exist in a dataset

sources.title: Scoring clarification: known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked (staff answers)
sources.role: binding scoring interpretation from the organisers
sources.used: Gapfinder objective: known pixels excluded from truth and penalty; halo parameter

claims.statement: The known-fault scoring mask is pixel-exact and identical to the supplied training labels.
claims.quote: The mask is indeed pixel-exact - it is identical to the provided set of training fault labels.

claims.statement: Known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels do not count towards penalty terms.
claims.quote: Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms.

claims.statement: A prediction near, but not on, a known trace is fully penalised unless near new-fault truth.
claims.quote: A predicted pixel that is near a known fault trace but far from a new-fault ground truth pixel will be fully penalized

claims.statement: New-fault truth can lie within 300 m of a known trace (corrections).
claims.quote: A new-fault ground truth pixel can indeed lie within 300m of a known fault trace.

sources.title: Where do you draw the line? - definition of a new fault (staff answer)
sources.role: binding target definition from the organisers

claims.statement: A new fault is any fault pixel not already captured by USGS/INGENIOUS, including new geometry of existing systems.
claims.quote: can include newly mapped geometry of an existing fault system

sources.title: How were the new test faults identified? (staff answer)
sources.role: states that test-label sources are not disclosed
sources.used: risk register: hidden-label type unknown, motivates source-robust selection

claims.statement: Organisers will not share data sources, fault types or coverage of the test faults.
claims.quote: We're not sharing details about the data sources, fault types, or coverage behind the test faults beyond what's in the problem description.
